<Route path="/ade/dashboard/versions" />

OpenAPI 3.2 adds four things a project's paths can hold:

| Construct | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **QUERY and custom methods** | The safe, body-bearing `QUERY` method (the Path Item's `query` field), and any other HTTP method such as `REPORT` or `LINK`, keyed by its token under `additionalOperations` |
| **Tag hierarchy** | A Tag Object's `summary`, its `parent` (another tag, so tags form a tree) and its `kind` (for example `nav`, `badge` or `audience`) |
| **Streaming media types** | A request body or response whose content is a stream — JSON Lines, JSON text sequences, Server-Sent Events — described one element at a time with `itemSchema` |
| **`in: querystring`** | A parameter that is the whole query string, given as one value with `content` (usually `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) |

A project keeps each of them when you import an OpenAPI 3.2 document. You can also add them with
the REST API, see them in the spec viewer and in version diffs, and get them back in OpenAPI 3.2
exports.

## Which documents show them

Each construct is written in the form the target version has:

| Construct | OpenAPI 3.2 | OpenAPI 3.1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QUERY operation | `query` | `x-apiome-query-operation` |
| Custom method | `additionalOperations.<METHOD>` | `x-apiome-additional-operations.<METHOD>` |
| Streaming media type | `itemSchema` | `x-apiome-item-schema` |
| `in: querystring` parameter | written | left out (3.1 has no such location) |
| Tag `summary`, `parent`, `kind` | written | left out (`name`, `description` and `externalDocs` stay) |

The `x-apiome-*` extensions are how a 3.1 document keeps an operation that 3.1 has no field for.
Importing that document brings the operations back. No 3.2 field ever appears in a 3.1 document.

The spec viewer and version diffs build OpenAPI 3.2, so they show every construct. For
**Export to another format…**, see [Export a spec](../ship/export-a-spec.md). That page also
explains how a 3.2 → 3.1 export lists each construct it could not keep.

## See them in the spec viewer

1. **Open the project** on **Versions**.
2. On the revision's row, **open the “Actions” menu** and **choose “View spec”**.
3. The dialog's title names the version the document declares (**OpenAPI 3.2.0 specification**).
   When the document uses any of the four constructs, **OpenAPI 3.2.0 constructs** above the code
   lists them, one group each:
   - **QUERY and custom methods** — the method, the path, the `operationId` and the field it is
     declared in (`query` or `additionalOperations`).
   - **Tag hierarchy** — each tag with a `parent`, `kind` or `summary`.
   - **Streaming media types** — the media type, its stream family and where it is.
   - **Query string parameters** — the operation, the parameter and its media type.

   A group with nothing in it is not shown. A 3.0 or 3.1 document has no panel.

<Screenshot id="openapi32-operations" alt="The spec viewer for Orders API 2.4.0, titled OpenAPI 3.2.0 specification: the OpenAPI 3.2.0 constructs panel lists QUERY /orders searchOrders and REPORT /orders reportOrders, the orders tag tree, two streaming media types and the filter query string parameter, above the JSON" />

Choose **YAML** to read the document's `tags` with their `parent` and `kind`:

<Screenshot id="openapi32-tags" alt="The same spec viewer in YAML: the Tag hierarchy group lists order-search and order-events under orders and beta of kind badge, and the code shows order-search with parent: orders and kind: nav" />

To see what changed between two revisions, compare them on **Versions** (see
[Versions](./versions.mdx)). A QUERY operation, a new `additionalOperations` method, a changed
`parent` or a new `itemSchema` shows as a line of the OpenAPI 3.2 document.

## With the REST API

Paths, operations, parameters and content types use the routes on
[Edit paths and operations](./edit-paths.md#with-the-rest-api).

### QUERY and custom methods

Create the operation with its method token. Any [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-tokens)
token is accepted; a space, a `/` or an empty method is refused with `422`.

```http
POST /v1/paths/{tenant_slug}/{version_id}/{path_id}/operations
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

{ "operation": "QUERY" }
```

`GET` … `TRACE` are the fixed verbs; `QUERY` is written as `query`; anything else (`REPORT`) goes
under `additionalOperations` with the token as you sent it. QUERY and custom methods keep their
request body, as POST, PUT and PATCH do.

### Streaming media types

Add the content type with `item_schema: true`. Its class or inline schema then describes **each
element** of the stream, not the whole body:

```http
POST /v1/paths/{tenant_slug}/{version_id}/{path_id}/responses/{response_id}/content-types
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

{ "media_type": "application/jsonl", "class_id": "<Order class id>", "item_schema": true }
```

The same field is on `…/request-bodies/{request_body_id}/content-types`. It defaults to `false`.

### `in: querystring`

Create the parameter with `in_location: "querystring"`. `data.contentMediaType` is its media type
(default `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`); the rest of `data` is the schema of the whole query
string:

```http
POST /v1/paths/{tenant_slug}/{version_id}/{path_id}/parameters
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

{
  "name": "filter",
  "in_location": "querystring",
  "data": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": { "status": { "type": "string" } },
    "contentMediaType": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
  }
}
```

`in_location` must be `path`, `query`, `header`, `cookie` or `querystring`.

### Tag hierarchy

A project's tags are one list, in document order:

| Action | Method & route |
|---|---|
| Read the tags | `GET /v1/projects/{tenant_slug}/{project_id}/openapi-tags` |
| Replace the tags | `PUT /v1/projects/{tenant_slug}/{project_id}/openapi-tags` |

```http
PUT /v1/projects/{tenant_slug}/{project_id}/openapi-tags
X-API-Key: <your-api-key>

{
  "tags": [
    { "name": "orders", "summary": "Orders", "description": "Everything about orders", "kind": "nav" },
    { "name": "order-search", "summary": "Search", "parent": "orders", "kind": "nav" },
    { "name": "beta", "kind": "badge" }
  ]
}
```

The list replaces the stored one, and `[]` clears it. The request is refused with `422`
(`invalid_tags`, one message per problem) when:

- a name is listed twice;
- a `parent` is the tag itself or names a tag that is not in the list;
- `parent` links form a cycle.

If someone else changed the project while you saved, the request returns `409` (`update_conflict`).
Read the tags again and retry. An OpenAPI import fills the same list from the document's `tags`.

## Verify

- **Spec viewer:** **View spec** on the revision lists the construct under **OpenAPI 3.2.0
  constructs**.
- **Round trip:** in the spec viewer, **click “Download”** and import the file into a new project
  (see [Import a spec](../bring-in/import-a-spec.md)). The new project's spec viewer lists the same
  operations, tags, streams and query string parameters.
